Third-Party Calibrations

The OpenCV and Kalibr lens conventions, the OpenCV and MATLAB calibration readers, the Schöps cameracalibration readers, the OpenCV-shaped writer, the migrations to native files, and the migration of an earlier schema version (`vgiomigrate,vgiomigratetree,migrate_schema`).

VisualGeometryToolkitIO.kalibr_lens — Method
kalibr_lens(camera_model, intrinsics, distortion_model, distortion_coeffs) -> (fx, fy, cx, cy, lens)

A Kalibr camchain camera (camera_model ∈ pinhole, omni, ds, eucm; distortion_model ∈ radtan, equidistant, fov, none) as its focal lengths, principal point and the VGC lens computing Kalibr's projection.

source
VisualGeometryToolkitIO.opencv_camera — Method
opencv_camera([file_frame = PixelFrame{:opencv},] K, dist) -> CameraModel

OpenCV's calibration — the camera matrix K (pixels, cx, cy in file_frame, OpenCV's own frame by default; no skew) and the distortion vector dist (opencv_lens: 4, 5, 8, 12 or 14 entries) — as a VGC CameraModel(LogicalIntrinsics(K′), lens) with K′'s principal point in the canonical COLMAP frame, moved by EuclideanMap(file_frame, PixelFrame{:colmap}). Inverse of opencv_parameters.

The round trip opencv_parameters(opencv_camera(K, dist)) returns K and dist bit for bit, with one exception that floating point forces: a principal point coordinate c ≥ ½ in [2ᵏ − ½, 2ᵏ) whose last mantissa bit is set (such as 511.75000000000006 or 2047.5000000000002) has no exact c + ½ (the sum needs one bit more than its binade holds), and comes back within one ulp of c (abs(c′ − c) == eps(c)). Every other c ≥ ½ — 511.5, 2047.5, any c with its last bit clear — comes back exactly. A file in another frame (PixelFrame{:julia}, whose map shifts by −½) round-trips exactly.

source
VisualGeometryToolkitIO.opencv_coefficients — Method
opencv_coefficients(lens) -> Vector{Float64}

OpenCV's distortion vector for a lens it computes: a perspective lens whose distortion is OpenCV's — a radial factor of at most three numerator and three denominator coefficients, tangential terms, a thin prism of at most two coefficients per axis, then a tilt — written as the shortest vector (4, 5, 8, 12 or 14 entries) holding all of it. Any other lens is refused.

source
VisualGeometryToolkitIO.opencv_lens — Method
opencv_lens(c::AbstractVector) -> Lens

The lens computing OpenCV's projectPoints distortion for the coefficient vector c = (k1, k2, p1, p2[, k3[, k4, k5, k6[, s1, s2, s3, s4[, τx, τy]]]]) — 4, 5, 8, 12 or 14 entries, the terms that length evaluates. Inverse of opencv_coefficients.

source
VisualGeometryToolkitIO.opencv_parameters — Method
opencv_parameters([to_frame = PixelFrame{:opencv},] camera) -> (; K, dist)

OpenCV's camera matrix K (cx, cy in to_frame, OpenCV's own by default) and distortion vector dist (opencv_coefficients) of a VGC camera whose lens OpenCV computes. Inverse of opencv_camera; a skewed K or a lens OpenCV does not compute is refused.

VisualGeometryToolkitIO.pose_covariance_from_ros — Method
pose_covariance_from_ros(Σ_ros) -> CovMat{6}

A ROS PoseWithCovariance covariance (x, y, z, rot X, rot Y, rot Z; a 6×6, or the message's row-major float64[36]) in the stack's order, rotation first — the covariance an Uncertain pose carries. Inverse of ros_pose_covariance.

source
VisualGeometryToolkitIO.ros_pose_covariance — Method
ros_pose_covariance(Σ) -> SMatrix{6, 6, Float64}

A pose covariance in the stack's order ([δω; δt], rotation first) as ROS PoseWithCovariance.covariance orders it (x, y, z, rot X, rot Y, rot Z): P·Σ·Pᵀ with P = [0 I; I 0]. Flatten row-major (vec(permutedims(Σ_ros))) for the message's float64[36]. Inverse of pose_covariance_from_ros.

VisualGeometryToolkitIO.ExternalCalibration — Type
ExternalCalibration{C <: CameraModel}

One third-party calibration file as read by load_opencv_calibration or load_matlab_calibration: source (:opencv or :matlab), camera (a VGC CameraModel, in the canonical frame by construction), poses (one VGC EuclideanMap labeled TargetFrame{target} → CameraFrame, its translation lengths in metres, per image; nothing where the file has null), the file's reprojection_error in pixels together with the statistic it is (error_statistic: :rms for OpenCV, :mean for MATLAB), path, and images: the image name of every pose when the file names them — this package's writer does — or nothing for a third-party export, whose positional join with the images is then the caller's.

A FOREIGN-FORMAT ADAPTER — the in-memory image of a third-party file, which VGIo reads and does not own — so it keeps its own type; everything it holds is a VGC value.

source
VisualGeometryToolkitIO.load_kalibr_camchain — Method
load_kalibr_camchain([file_frame = PixelFrame{:opencv},] path; camera = "cam0") -> BoundedCamera

One camera of a Kalibr camchain (camchain.yaml of kalibr_calibrate_cameras): its camera_model × distortion_model as kalibr_lens maps them, its intrinsics (focal lengths and principal point) and its resolution, as a BoundedCamera in VGC's canonical (COLMAP) pixel frame. file_frame is the pixel frame of the file's principal point, which Kalibr does not write: its projection is OpenCV's, PixelFrame{:opencv}, the default. The extrinsics of a multi-camera chain (T_cn_cnm1) are not read.

source
VisualGeometryToolkitIO.load_matlab_calibration — Method
load_matlab_calibration([file_frame = PixelFrame{:julia},] path; file_unit, target = "calibration_target")
    -> ExternalCalibration

Read a MATLAB Computer Vision Toolbox calibration export. The radial/tangential files (fx, fy, cx, cy, r1, r2, r3, t1, t2) state OpenCV's polynomial term for term, so the camera is OpenCV's five-coefficient model, opencv_lens([r1, r2, t1, t2, r3]). The fisheye file (mapping_coeffs, distortion_center, stretch_matrix, MATLAB's fisheyeIntrinsics) is Scaramuzza's model: the sensor-plane point (u′, v′) reaches the image as stretch_matrix · (u′, v′) + distortion_center and back-projects to the ray (u′, v′, a0 + a2·ρ² + a3·ρ³ + a4·ρ⁴) in the sensor-plane pixel radius ρ, so a0 is the focal length, the stretch and the centre are K, and the polynomial normalized by a0 is VGC's Scaramuzza (aᵢ ↦ aᵢ·a0^(i−1)). K must be upper triangular and the stretch matrix is not: its RQ factorization S = U·Q puts a0·U in K and Q, a rotation of the sensor plane, into the camera frame — a rotation about the optical axis (a fraction of a degree on this capture) that every returned pose carries, so the camera and its poses stay one consistent model. That rotation is part of the difference between this camera's frame and an OpenCV fit's, and shows in a mount compared across the two. mean_error is the file's statistic — a MEAN reprojection error, not an rms (error_statistic == :mean).

file_frame is the pixel frame of the file's centre and principal point: MATLAB's documented convention, PixelFrame{:julia} (top-left pixel centre at (1, 1)), by default — a fitted principal point cannot tell it from an exporter's shift to OpenCV's, so override it only for a file verified to be in another frame. file_unit is the world unit the toolbox was given the pattern in (mm for a pattern typed in millimetres) — tvec is in it; there is no default. MATLAB's board frame has x and y exchanged relative to OpenCV's for the same pattern: the poses are returned in MATLAB's own board frame, so name its target apart from an OpenCV calibration's. target names the pattern in the pose records (target → camera_optical).

source
VisualGeometryToolkitIO.load_opencv_calibration — Method
load_opencv_calibration([file_frame = PixelFrame{:opencv},] path; file_unit, target = "calibration_target")
    -> ExternalCalibration

Read an OpenCV calibration export: fx, fy, cx, cy; the distortion vector by name — k1, k2, p1, p2 required, k3–k6, s1–s4 and the tilt tilt_x, tilt_y (OpenCV's τx, τy) as the file names them — read as the lens computing OpenCV's model for the shortest distortion vector holding every named coefficient (opencv_lens), the unnamed ones zero; an unknown key is refused, never ignored (a dropped tilt would be a different camera); rms in pixels; poses, one {rvec, tvec} per image (null allowed); and images, the name of each pose's image, when the file names them (this package's writer does; a third-party export does not, and its join with the images is positional and the caller's).

The two arguments are statements about the FILE — what a third-party export does not declare — never labels on data: file_unit is the length unit of tvec (the object points' unit, m or mm), and file_frame the pixel frame of cx, cy, OpenCV's own PixelFrame{:opencv} by default (a type, it leads). The camera returned is in VGC's canonical frame by construction and the poses' translations lengths (metres), so nothing downstream restates either. target names the pattern in the pose records (target → camera_optical).

Most third-party exports declare neither and are read as stated; some declare tvec_unit. A file written by save_opencv_calibration declares both (unit, image_origin), and a declaration that differs from the caller's is an ArgumentError, never a silent rescale: a metre file read as millimetres puts every target a thousand times too near.

source
VisualGeometryToolkitIO.save_opencv_calibration — Method
save_opencv_calibration([to_frame = PixelFrame{:opencv},] path, camera, poses; rms, to_unit, images)
save_opencv_calibration([to_frame = PixelFrame{:opencv},] path, cal::ExternalCalibration; to_unit, images = cal.images)

Write an OpenCV-shaped calibration export — THE INVERSE of load_opencv_calibration, and the only writer for that shape, so the two cannot drift: fx, fy, cx, cy, the twelve distortion coefficients by name (k1–k6, p1, p2, s1–s4, each written even when zero, which is what makes a default, rational or thin-prism fit one file shape), rms in pixels, one {rvec, tvec} per image — null for an image with no pose — and images, the name of each pose's image, REQUIRED: a positional join with an image list kept elsewhere is exactly the out-of-band knowledge a file must not need.

The shape is a THIRD-PARTY one, so its conventions are its consumer's, and the two arguments are CONVERSION TARGETS applied to data whose own conventions its types fix — the camera's K is canonical by VGC's construction, the poses' translations are lengths — never labels for it:

to_frame the pixel frame cx, cy are written in; OpenCV's own, PixelFrame{:opencv}, by default. A type, it leads. to_unit the length unit tvec is written in (write_length: a pose 1.39719 m from the target is tvec 1.39719 in m, 1397.19 in mm). A plain translation is an ArgumentError.

Both are also written into the file, under image_origin and unit, and the reader refuses a caller who states different ones.

camera must carry a lens OpenCV's distortion model computes (opencv_coefficients); the file names the coefficients of the shortest OpenCV vector holding it. A K with nonzero skew is refused: the shape has no field for it.

source
VisualGeometryToolkitIO.SCHOEPS_PIXEL_FRAME — Type
SCHOEPS_PIXEL_FRAME

The pixel frame of Schöps et al.'s camera_calibration files: origin at the top-left corner of the top-left pixel, so pixel (i, j)'s centre is (i + ½, j + ½) — PixelFrame{:colmap} exactly (the identity EuclideanMap(PixelFrame{:colmap}, PixelFrame{:colmap})).

VisualGeometryToolkitIO._migrate_cli — Method
_migrate_cli(args; io = stdout) -> Int

The bin/vgio_migrate.jl command: opencv|matlab [options] FILE (a third-party calibration), target|rig|file [options] FILE, tree [options] DIR and repoint [options] FILE (earlier schema versions), each a dry run unless --apply. Returns the process exit code: 0 on success, 1 when the conversion failed, 2 on a usage error.

source
VisualGeometryToolkitIO.migrate_matlab — Method
migrate_matlab([file_frame = PixelFrame{:julia},] path; images, image_size, file_unit = nothing,
               target = "calibration_target", out = dirname(path), dry_run = false) -> NamedTuple

Convert a third-party MATLAB calibration export (calibration_matlab_*.json: the radial/tangential camera fx, fy, cx, cy, r1…r3, t1, t2, or the fisheye mapping_coeffs, distortion_center, stretch_matrix; mean_error; one {rvec, tvec} per image) into the same native files as migrate_opencv, which it mirrors: <stem>_cameras.json (the camera as load_matlab_calibration reads it — MATLAB's polynomial lens, or the fisheye as Scaramuzza with its stretch in K; provenance records the reprojection_error with error_statistic = "mean", MATLAB's statistic, not an rms) and <stem>_poses.json (target:<target> → view:<image> per posed image, in the export's tvec unit — the fisheye's frame twist applied, as the reader applies it). The original is never touched, and the round trip is verified before anything is written.

file_frame defaults to MATLAB's documented pixel convention, the top-left pixel's centre at (1, 1) (PixelFrame{:julia}); override it only for a calibration VERIFIED to be in another frame. file_unit is REQUIRED unless the file declares its tvec unit (the toolbox's exports do not; its tvec is in the unit the pattern was given in — millimetres for this stack's captures). MATLAB's board frame has x and y exchanged relative to OpenCV's for the same pattern, and the poses are carried in MATLAB's own board frame, unchanged: give target a name that keeps them apart from an OpenCV calibration's.

source
VisualGeometryToolkitIO.migrate_opencv — Method
migrate_opencv([file_frame = PixelFrame{:opencv},] path; images, image_size,
               file_unit = nothing, target = "calibration_target",
               out = dirname(path), dry_run = false) -> NamedTuple

Convert a third-party OpenCV calibration export (calibration_opencv_*.json: fx, fy, cx, cy, named distortion coefficients, rms, one {rvec, tvec} per image) into native files (cameras v3, transforms v2), where everything the export leaves implicit is declared. The original is never touched. Written to out:

  • <stem>_cameras.json — a vgio/cameras/v3 store holding one camera named <stem>: width/height from image_size, K in the canonical pixel frame, and the lens record of opencv_lens for the export's distortion vector (the terms its length evaluates). The export's reprojection statistic is its provenance (reprojection_error, error_statistic = "rms", source = "opencv", migrated_from).
  • <stem>_poses.json — a vgio/transforms/v2 file, one record per image the solver posed, NAMED by that image: from = "target:<target>", to = "view:<image>" — the target in the camera frame of that view, x_view = R x_target + t, in the export's tvec unit (declared as its length_unit). An image whose pose the export has as null has no record.

images is REQUIRED — one unique, non-empty name per entry of the export's poses, in the export's order — and replaces the positional join the export leaves to its reader. image_size (width, height) is required because a camera is not sufficient without its extent and an OpenCV export does not record it.

file_unit is the unit of tvec: taken from the file's tvec_unit (or this package's own unit) when it declares one — and then a stated file_unit must agree — and otherwise REQUIRED; there is no default.

file_frame is the pixel frame of cx, cy, and the ONLY place a pixel frame is stated by hand: by the user's rule OpenCV's own, the top-left pixel's centre at (0, 0) (PixelFrame{:opencv}). Override it only for a calibration VERIFIED to be in another frame. A type, it leads, as a type does in a non-mutating call. Everything downstream carries the frame in its type: the camera read is canonical by construction, and the files declare what their types say.

The conversion is verified before anything is written to out: the v2 files, written to a staging directory beside out (a dry run's: a temporary one) and renamed into place only once verified, must read back equal to the OpenCV read — the camera ==, every pose's translation bit for bit (a file-born value; a computed one within the length conversion's 2 ulp) and its rotation to the quaternion encoding's precision (_qvec). With dry_run nothing is written to out. Returns (; path, cameras, poses, n_posed, n_unposed), the output paths nothing in a dry run.

VisualGeometryToolkitIO.migrate_schema — Function
migrate_schema(::Val{schema}, src, dst) -> NamedTuple

The migration of a file of the (old) schema — a Symbol, Val(Symbol("vgio/rig/v4")) — at src into its kind's current schema, written to dst (a path in the staging directory vgio_migrate owns). A method reads src, writes the current file to dst through its writer, reads dst back with the current reader and compares every number with src (a length as its value, within the length conversion's 2-ulp guarantee), throwing an ArgumentError on any difference; it returns a summary NamedTuple with at least to, the schema written (and whatever the owner reports: a rig's old_id and new_id).

A declared extension point (VisualGeometryToolkitIO's CONTRACT_GENERICS): the owner of a schema adds the method for each of its old versions. VisualGeometryToolkitIO's own: vgio/target/v1 → vgio/target/v2 and vgio/rig/v4 → vgio/rig/v5.

source
VisualGeometryToolkitIO.vgio_migrate — Method
vgio_migrate(path; out = <stem>.migrated.json beside path, dry_run = false) -> NamedTuple

Migrate the file at path from the earlier schema version it declares to its kind's current one, by the method of migrate_schema for that schema (vgio/target/v1, vgio/rig/v4, and any a schema owner adds). The migration is written through the current writer to a staging directory BESIDE out (the same filesystem), read back with the current reader and compared with the original, number for number; only then is it renamed to out, one atomic rename. Every number comes back bit for bit except a length (or a covariance entry of lengths) the file holds at full precision, 16 or 17 digits: no metre value writes back to every such number, so the migrated file may hold one that differs by at most 2 ulp — reading back as the same metre value, within the length conversion's 2-ulp guarantee (read_length). A number of at most 15 significant digits is rewritten as its own text. The original is untouched unless out == path (an in-place migration, replaced by that rename only once verified); an existing out is otherwise refused. With dry_run the migration is verified and nothing is written. Returns (; path, out, from, to, …), out nothing in a dry run, with whatever the schema's migration reports — a rig's old_ids (the v4 identities measurement files may name it by: the one hashed from the file as written, and the one v4 minted for the value in millimetres, when the file is in another unit) and its new_id.

source
VisualGeometryToolkitIO.vgio_migrate_tree — Method
vgio_migrate_tree(dir; in_place = false, dry_run = false, io = stdout) -> Vector{NamedTuple}

Migrate every .json file under dir whose schema has a migration (a vgio/target/v1, a vgio/rig/v4, and any schema whose owner added a migrate_schema method), then re-point the measurement files under dir (vgio/target_points2d/v1, vgio/target_points3d/v1) at the current rigs of the tree, each by the guarded pattern of vgio_migrate (a full-precision length may be rewritten within 2 ulp, as the same metre value), with one line per file to io — a file left as it is says why (current, or no targets). Written beside each original as <stem>.migrated.json, or over it with in_place.

The re-pointing is a one-time consequence of the rig/v4 → v5 migration: the v4 identity hashed the record's format, the v5 one does not, so each migrated rig's old identities map to its new one. The map is PERSISTED in dir/vgio_migrate_ids.json before a rig is put in place, and read by a later run, so a run that fails after its rigs were migrated in place re-points correctly when rerun; a rerun of a migrated tree is idempotent (every file current, logged so). A file the migration refuses — its migration does not read back, its <stem>.migrated.json exists and is not current, a measurement file names an identity that is neither mapped nor a current rig's of the tree, or a measurement does not resolve in its rigs — is logged FAILED with the reason, nothing is written for it, and the run goes on with the other files; it then ends in ONE ArgumentError listing every refusal.

source
VisualGeometryToolkitIO.write_staged — Method
write_staged(f, out => name, …; dry_run) -> f's result

Write files through a staging directory, the guarded pattern of every migration: f(staged...) is called with one path per out => name (each named name, in a fresh directory BESIDE the destinations, so on their filesystem) and builds and verifies the files there; then, unless a dry_run, each is put at its out by one rename, in the order given — atomic on POSIX, so an original at out is untouched until its rename, and nothing is moved across filesystems. The destinations share one directory, created if missing (an ArgumentError otherwise, before anything is written). A dry run stages in a temporary directory and puts nothing anywhere. The staging directory goes when this returns, whatever happened. On a failure — f throws, or a rename does — the destinations are left as they were: a destination that did not exist and was already renamed into place is removed again (one that existed was replaced by its rename and stays so), and a directory this call created for them is removed.
